entries.name: the Barrow of the Fallen
entries.summary: The Barrow of the Fallen, a mound a little outside town with a sealed way from the temple: the wealthy town's newer dead on its top floor, the ancient dead moved down to the Ossuary, the oldest to a damp, dark third layer, and the draugr's Hall of Fallen Souls; grave robbers plunder it, and the temple's alms go down to keep the upper tombs quiet (docs/lore/crypt.md; decision 546, npc's side, part 3: the [Jeff] rows; lore adds the [proposal] rows).

facts.text: The crypt is a place to keep away from.
The town's first folk moved the old dead down to make room for their own, the oldest as far down as they dared go.
Only the wealthy are laid in the barrow; the poor lie in paupers' graves outside.
The barrow's top floor holds the town's newer dead.
Below the barrow's top floor lies the Ossuary, where the ancient dead were moved.
The barrow's third layer, where the oldest dead lie, is damp and dark, too moist for any lamp to burn.
Grave robbers plunder the barrow, and the dead below do not know them from anyone else who comes down.
The dead below are angry at being disturbed, and the draugr's magic moves them.
The draugr keeps the Hall of Fallen Souls, at the bottom of the barrow.
Ghostly warriors fill the Hall of Fallen Souls, promised an eternal feast and battle.
The temple's alms go down to the dead, to keep the upper tombs quiet.
The draugr bargains for gold.
The door of the Hall of Fallen Souls closes behind whoever enters, and opens again for gold returned or for his defeat.
Carrying the Draugr's Totem gives its holder another chance to fight.
Pip carries the temple's offering down to the altar in the barrow.
The Barrow of the Fallen lies a little outside town, under a grass-covered mound with a stone-framed door.
Warriors' spears are planted around the outside of the mound, standing up like spikes.
